note: Anglo-Scottish relations from the Norman Conquest (1066) through the medieval period were defined by English attempts at dominance and Scottish resistance. The Wars of Scottish Independence (1296–1357) — triggered by Edward I's attempt to make Scotland an English vassal — produced William Wallace, Robert Bruce, and the Declaration of Arbroath (1320). The 1328 Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton recognized Scottish independence. The 'Auld Alliance' with France defined Scottish policy throughout the Hundred Years' War. Periodic warfare continued until the Union of Crowns (1603).

_quarry.structural_significance: Defines Scottish national identity through resistance to English dominance; the Wars of Independence create Scotland's foundational political mythology; the Auld Alliance shapes French-English-Scottish triangular diplomacy for 300 years
